note: Parameters read BY EYE from the registered body (colour bands per row) on 2026-09-25; derive_r2.py applies them.

split_body.why: the belt's grey rows run y 730-790 (measured grey-row profile)

helmet_front.why: helmet_front r2 is cut from the MASTER's pixels (no seam at rest). zone_px: search band around the registered helmet; palette_margin: a pixel is head only when its colour is nearer the head palette by this much (shell shading stays helmet); ink_px: outline within this distance of helmet colour is helmet; fill_reach_px: master pixels next to the helmet that head_no_helmet does not cover are kept so the stack has no hole

head_blank_refit.why: r1 registered head_blank at s 0.345 onto the eye (visibly tiny, reviewed); r2 fits it to the registered head_no_helmet instead: s 0.656, overlay reviewed (cranium, snout and neck coincide)

edge_to_master.why: r2.1 (verifier: 'torso 12-16 px wider on the image-right side, rows 560-840, 7862 px outside'): measured per layer, that overhang is the far sleeve arm_left (x 759 vs 743 at y 720), plus the body's collar and shoulders above it; what shows at rest outside the master's silhouette is trimmed and the new edge takes the master's own outline pixels (band_px). Hidden overlap under the layers in front is kept for rotation

lower_from_master.why: r2.1 (verifier): the r2 coat_tails cut from the registered body redraw sat 8 px low (best shift dx +1, dy -8) and 30 px too wide per side at y 920; the legs sat 3 px low with boots 8-13 px narrower than the master. No hand overlaps the coat or the legs, so both are cut from the master's own pixels (cells assigned to the registered slots), the coat from the master's belt middle line down, the legs with their hidden tops extended under the coat
